applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations (northwest, west-central, east-central, south-central)
findings.comment: Transformer pads shown with dashed clearance rectangles on electrical plan, but no specific clearance dimensions are annotated. Cannot verify 5-foot minimum clearance from buildings without dimensioned measurements or cross-reference to building elevations.

Transformer equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on electrical plans. The 12-foot horizontal clearance requirement from windows/doors applies only to oil-filled equipment with less than 12 feet lateral separation or low grade elevation. Without transformer type identification and window/door elevation documentation, compliance cannot be verified.

Northwest and west-central transformer pads appear positioned very close to proposed 5-foot sidewalks on the western property edge, but exact clearance dimension is not provided on plans. Cannot confirm 2-foot minimum separation without specific measurement.

Hot-stick use area clearance boundary is indicated by dashed rectangles on electrical plan extending in appropriate direction (west for Pads 1-3, south for Pad 4), but no specific 10-foot dimension is annotated. Cannot verify compliance without dimensioned measurements.

Tree list provided with species identification, but transformer pad locations are not explicitly marked or dimensioned on landscape plan. Cannot determine which trees (if any) fall within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment or 15 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors. Tree plan and electrical plan cannot be cross-referenced due to missing transformer pad overlay on landscape sheet.

Landscape plan shows extensive vegetation and shrub plantings throughout site, but transformer pad locations are not shown on the landscape plan. Cannot verify shrub clearances (10 lateral feet from access door side, 5 lateral feet from other sides) without explicit transformer location reference on landscape sheet.

No root barrier details shown anywhere on landscape sheets. Transformer pad locations not marked on landscape plan, so cannot identify which trees (if any) fall within 20 lateral feet requiring root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from equipment).

Water utility lines shown on utility plan in general site vicinity, but specific clearance distances from transformer pads are not dimensioned. Cannot verify 5-foot horizontal minimum clearance without measured distances.
Wastewater utility routing shown on utility tap plan, but specific clearance distances from transformer pads not dimensioned. Cannot verify 5-foot horizontal minimum clearance requirement.

applicableAreas: East-central transformer pad and other locations
findings.comment: Storm drain line routing shown on utility and electrical plans and appears in close proximity to east-central transformer pad (possibly within 5 feet based on visual scale), but exact distance is not dimensioned. Cannot verify 5-foot horizontal minimum clearance.

Underground utility lines (electric, water, wastewater, storm drain) shown in general site layout, but specific 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance distances from transformer pads not documented on plans. Cannot verify separation without dimensioned measurements.

Utility routing and building locations shown but no documentation provided confirming transformer pads do not have utilities or building foundations crossing above or under pad locations. Spatial relationship not explicitly verified on plans.

applicableAreas: East-central and south-central transformer pads (immediately adjacent to Buildings 4 and 7)
findings.comment: East-central transformer pad is immediately adjacent to Building 4 wall; south-central pad is immediately adjacent to Building 7 wall. These enclosed structures/buildings above or adjacent to transformer locations require cross-section drawings demonstrating vertical clearances in access paths, but no cross-sections are provided on the plan set.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations, particularly west-central pad in drainage corridor
findings.comment: Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on electrical plans. Drainage requirement (liquid flow away from building) applies only to oil-filled equipment. Grading analysis shows west-central pad located in localized drainage corridor/swale with water flowing through area, which would be problematic for oil-filled equipment. Without transformer type identification, compliance cannot be verified.

Facts.md documents that several recorded easements (Greenbelt Access & Use, City of Austin Drainage, Public Utility Easements, and others) are not depicted on submitted site plan. Transformer pads' locations relative to all recorded easements cannot be verified without complete easement documentation on plans. Cannot confirm pads are outside drainage easements, water easements, sewer easements, and electrical easements under overhead lines.

Electrical plan does not explicitly show transformer easement boundaries or dimensions around pads. Site plan notes indicate additional electric easements may be required, but specific transformer easement widths and accessibility requirements determined by Austin Energy Design are not documented on preliminary plans.

applicableAreas: Electrical routing from all transformer pads to meters
findings.comment: Electrical routing lines shown on electrical plan connecting to buildings and meters, but specific confirmation that 100% of routing is on private property (not crossing easements or public right-of-way) is not documented on plans.

Transformer pads are shown on electrical plan with label and location, but no Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets are provided. Transformer pad dimensions (length x width) are not specified. Service type (single-phase vs. three-phase) is not identified. These required design specifications must be obtained from Austin Energy Design and shown on construction documents.

applicableAreas: Northwest transformer pad (west of Bldg. 2); West-central transformer pad (between Bldg. 2 and 8)
findings.comment: Northwest and west-central transformer pads are positioned within 4 feet of parking area and vehicle circulation driveway curb. Bollards (4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts) are required per AE Design equipment pad details but are not shown for these two pads. Bollards are correctly shown for east-central and south-central pads which are similarly positioned relative to driveways.
